title: 2026 election news: Early voting draws steady turnout as Illinois governor candidates JB Pritzker, Darrien Bailey make final push - ABC7 Chicago

2026 election news: Early voting draws steady turnout as Illinois governor candidates JB Pritzker, Darrien Bailey make final push - ABC7 Chicago 
 24/7 Live Chicago & Suburban Cook Co. North Suburbs West Suburbs South Suburbs NW Indiana Midterm Elections 
 Early voting draws steady turnout as candidates make final push before Election Day 
 With two days remaining before Election Day, politicians made their final pitch to voters Sunday. WLS By Craig Wall Sunday, November 1, 2026 11:49PM Share CHICAGO (WLS) -- With two days remaining before Election Day, politicians made their final pitch to voters Sunday while residents across Chicago and the suburbs headed to early voting locations to cast their ballots.
 Voters face decisions on state, local and national races, including contests that could affect the balance of power in Congress.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Among those voting Sunday was 108-year-old Wheaton resident Nancy Rossi, who cast her ballot in person at the DuPage County Fairgrounds.
 "My birthday is April 10, 1918, and I live with my daughter," Rossi said.
 Rossi said she stopped voting for 40 years because of her disillusionment with political corruption. Asked how grateful she was to be able to cast a ballot, Rossi replied, "Oh, greatly, greatly, greatly."
 Her daughter, Carmine Pollack, said voting is now very important to Rossi.
 "She said we have to vote because if we don't vote, we can't complain," Pollack said.
 Rossi was among many voters who took advantage of shorter lines on Sunday.
 Donna Ciszczon, a DuPage County election judge supervisor, said turnout has been unusually strong.

 "Voter turnout this midterm is probably one of the largest I've seen in the last 10 years. Surprisingly enough, both mail-in ballots as well as in-person voting, and I'm just very surprised at how large it's been," Ciszczon said.
 According to the ABC7 early voting ballot tracker, turnout in DuPage County stood at 21.4%, nearly five percentage points higher than the state average. Chicago's turnout was 13.4%, both figures include both early voting and returned mail ballots.
 Gov. JB Pritzker spent part of Sunday campaigning at the Apostolic Church of God, where he invoked the late Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr. while encouraging supporters to participate in the election.
 "I come here humbly to make one request of all of you: do what he called on each of us to do. Keep hope alive, and vote," Pritzker said.
 Republican gubernatorial candidate Darren Bailey, who was spending time with family Sunday, emphasized the importance of turnout during a campaign stop earlier in the week.
 "If we learned anything from four years ago, that was what we learned. Just low voter turnout doesn't win elections, and we've been diligent in refining our message to affordability, safety, and education. We're sticking with that," Bailey said.
 Many voters said they were motivated by a desire to make their voices heard.
 "I want to make sure that my vote counts because I have kids and I have grandkids, and I want to make sure that their future is prosperous and just just a better living, just a better life," voter Shaira Manning said.
 Election officials said Sunday brought a steady stream of voters to polling locations, and they expect activity to increase during the final two days before Election Day.
